My Unexpected Journey to Hormone Replacement (TRT)

📅 16 Dec 2025 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2750 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.
  • In a recent development, but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here.
  • I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As a man of Science, I’m supposed to hide my enthusiasm about this somewhat controversial subject, and instead direct you only to the peer-reviewed studies.

In a recent development, but man, I feel like I’ve stumbled upon the fountain of youth here. And the more I dig into the details and the hype and controversy surrounding the field of Hormone Replacement therapy, the more I need to share the word about it to my fellow middle-aged people (both men and women).

I’ve been interested in optimization and trying to get the most out of my body and mind since I was a little kid. I started vacuuming up all the training and nutrition books and magazines I could find while I was just a teenager, and that field still remains a favorite of mine over 30 years later. And if you’re a long-time reader here you’ve been reminded plenty of times of this interest, because health has always been the very heart of Mustachianism.

Recent findings suggest that but a funny thing has been happening in the last ten years: even as I kept honing the healthy living habits and trying my best to improve, there seemed to be a force pulling me back almost as hard. So despite working a bit harder and smarter every year, I still felt myself riding a gradually declining tide of energy, motivation, and physical stamina.

“Perhaps this is just what it means to grow old”, I thought to myself,.

“But I’m still gonna keep fighting it!”.

Yet there was one thing that didn’t quite fit. Why was I having this decline in energy, when some of my older friends weren’t? And why was I still seeing people out there in their 50s, 60s and well beyond doing things that I felt too tired to do today?

In a recent development, one of these tireless friends is a guy named Kevin, who is the personification of the highly energetic successful middle-aged man. He’s a semi-retired serial entrepreneur (and extreme rock climber) who lives in Boulder. And through an interesting twist of fate, in April of 2025 he invited me out for a hike right around the time I was doing all this wondering. And during this hike (and climb) he told me about his latest venture, a boutique men’s health organization that specializes in helping men just like us get their youth back through the process of testosterone replacement therapy.

Long story short: his ideas planted a seed in my head, which led to a bunch of research and a growing interest in trying TRT myself. I had of course heard about the process, but for some reason never considered doing it until I heard Kevin’s enthusiasm: he had been on it for several years, and according to him it is a “night and day difference” in all the things you want in life: energy, focus, thinking speed, and of course physical health.

It has been revealed that another convenient twist of fate is that I happen to be dating an REI doctor – a Reproductive Endocrinologist and Infertility specialist who has two board certifications in exactly the relevant bodily systems that are affected by these hormones. And while she was initially skeptical that I needed more Testosterone (and in her practice she regularly sees the downsides of men taking the stuff too early in life and thus compromising their own fertility), she has followed along and helped me learn at each step of this process, eventually becoming fully in support of the program.

It has been revealed that so I signed up as a test customer for Kevin’s new firm, which is called Bolt Health. I worked with their doctor to get a baseline blood test and review my numbers compared to all the past tests I’ve collected, and as it turned out, my levels had been dropping consistently over the years, and the latest test was by far the lowest ever.

Even more telling, my age-related drop in Testosterone was correlating perfectly with my decline in energy and motivation:.

The next step was a prescription for a tiny daily dose of supplemental T, which arrived at my house the next week along with instructions for how to use it. And so began the journey.

Now let’s jump forward seven months to the present day as I write this.

Recent findings suggest that and wow, what a great year it has been! I only wish I had known and tried this a few years earlier, because I’m getting a lot more out of my life.

Industry observers note that it’s not a night-and-day difference for me, but more like a 50% boost in overall youthfulness and energy. The biggest subjective change is that I just don’t have sucky tired days anymore, which was the main problem with my life before: wasting too much of my precious freedom due to not having the energy to enjoy it.

In a recent development, this is why I’ve become somewhat of an evangelist for hormone replacement therapy for people from about age 45 onwards. It won’t work for everyone – if your levels are already pretty high, you don’t get the same boost. Two of my male friends tried TRT and quit because they didn’t notice any benefit. But these same two guys already had plenty of energy to begin with, which is usually a sign that the body has what it needs.

Recent findings suggest that it turns out I am very late to this party. Although Testosterone supplementation started out as a niche practice in the 1940s, from the 2010s onward it has been everywhere.

TRT is the reason you see every actor suddenly showing up buff overnight for their superhero roles and it’s also why so many of today’s CEOs don’t look anything like yesterday’s CEOs.

In many cases, it has gone too far with young men using it just to gain muscle for the beach or the football field, and questionable online providers (aka “Prescription Mills”) handing out prescriptions to anyone with a valid credit card – with profit as their sole motive. It became overhyped in certain pockets of Bro Culture, where every Bro eventually receives the advice “Bro! You need to get on the T!” from another Bro, and therefore does it. And some of this reputation surely contributed to my own skepticism.

But there’s a lot of valid science behind TRT, if you’re the right candidate and you take the right dosage. And because of that, I feel it is probably under-hyped in my own demographic, the Nerdy Tech Worker Semi Retired Dad contingent. And that’s why I’m writing this blog post, because there are a lot of us out there.

According to recent reports, many of us just tend to work with what we were given, and accept that aging means slowing down. And for those of us already enjoying an early retirement, we have the option of unlimited rest and recuperation time, so who really cares if we get tired a bit more often? After all, what better way to flex one’s wealth than with a decadent Tuesday Afternoon Nap while everyone else is stuck in the office?

While this seemingly healthy attitude has a lot of positive aspects, it can also mask a real problem which may be easily fixable. Because sometimes, the only thing that’s even better than an afternoon nap, is having the energy and motivation to go out for an afternoon hike, bike ride or adventure with friends. More energy is also pretty darned useful if you’re still raising kids or trying to do well in your career as a person over 45.

How it Actually Works (and What Happened to Me).

Recent findings suggest that distilling all of the fluffy discussion above into the simplest possible answer: TRT means using a tiny needle to inject a few drops of clear liquid just below the surface of your skin. And you do this by yourself at home, ideally once every morning.

Here’s one of the baby needles I use for my daily dose.The typical serving is less than one tenth of a milliliter, which is only a few drops.

Industry observers note that and while the term “needle” sounds scary to some, this is very different from the monstrosities they use to draw blood from your veins. This one is so miniature that you don’t need special training to use it, and you usually don’t even feel it.

It has been revealed that so I began doing this to myself on May 1st of this year, while keeping a daily journal of my results along the way. The results seemed to be almost immediate in all the promised areas, but I know how powerful the Placebo Effect can be so I kept my skeptic’s hat on to see what would happen in the long run.

It has been revealed that I was seeing increased energy and motivation as well as lean weight gain through the whole spring and summer, but I remember the first truly shocking observation happened during a mountain vacation in July. I was part of a multi-family trip with lively adults, chaotic kids, early mornings, late nights with a few drinks, very intense high altitude sunshine and nonstop physical activities. It was just the type of situation that would drain my energy pretty quickly in the past.

In a recent development, but on day three I went out on a solo mountain bike ride to explore the area, and as I was climbing a long ascent with the blazing sun cooking me from every angle I just somehow kept having plenty of energy to keep climbing. Then I came down and joined the group for a few games of full-sun pickleball, biked back up the mountain to our cabin, and the story of unlimited energy went on from there.

“Hot Damn”, I thought to myself, “I don’t know whose youthful and tireless body I have inherited here but I’d sure like to keep it!”.

In August, the Bolt Health program scheduled a follow-up blood test for me and sure enough, my Testosterone levels had been boosted from 415 to 730ng/dL, bringing me from the low side of normal to the higher side.

It has been revealed that many labs define “normal” as anywhere between 300 and 1000, which seems strange to me given the huge effect this hormone has on your wellbeing. It’s a bit like saying “Most cars have between 90 and 300 horsepower, so it doesn’t really matter what engine you have”.

I mean yeah, either one will still get you down the road, but which one would you rather be driving?

Sources indicate that since then, it has just been more of the same good results. My improvements ramped up and then just stayed there – so I’m operating at a new, much higher and more enjoyable level of functioning. Energy and motivation are no longer a problem, and I even find myself willing to make longer-term looks again (before this everything beyond same-day planning felt overwhelming). And my body seems to just want to gain strength and size with any excuse. Heavy weights feel lighter and the hard manual labor I still like to spend my time on feels easier for longer. It’s nice to be young again!

So Why Doesn’t Everyone Do This?

Recent findings suggest that when you dig into the details, hormone replacement is mired in a soup of both real and incorrect information about both its benefits and its risks. And then our well-meaning medical establishment locks this whole container of soup deep in the cabinet with a label that indicates, “Needs Further Study”. But if you summarize the findings on both sides of the issue, you’ll see this:.

Stuff you should do BEFORE trying TRT:.

The modern American Lifestyle is a Testosterone and Health Crusher. It’s a miracle that anybody feels good ever with the crap that people do to their bodies. So if you’re not already doing all the simple, natural, outdoor things that naturally boost your health, energy, and hormone levels, you’ll want to start with these first. You can find a pretty complete list on my oft-cited Badassity Tracker page.

Recent findings suggest that since I was already doing all of these things pretty consistently, I felt ready to take the next step and at least consider hormone supplementation. But wait, there’s more!

Many of the problems above are more likely to appear when the body is flooded with too much testosterone. In the bad old days, TRT was administered by sticking a pellet beneath your skin or injecting a large amount into the butt which then gets used up over the next several weeks. One friend recounted a story of extreme moodiness when the pellet was first implanted, ramping down to tiredness by the time the hormone was all gone.

More modern providers like Bolt have fixed this problem by breaking the dose into much smaller servings which you administer each day. The idea is that your levels remain stable, and you need a lot less overall which reduces side effects.

For my part, I have not had any of the negative side effects because I was a pretty ideal candidate in the first place: 50 years old with depressed Testosterone levels but an otherwise healthy lifestyle and no risk factors.

Sources indicate that my hope in sharing this article is to be transparent and hopefully take some of the stigma out of this subject of other people who might benefit. Because in our modern over-connected world, everybody has an opinion on your life, even when you didn’t ask them.

And it’s not just men – many women in this same age group benefit from Estrogen replacement (and there are even interesting stories about female testosterone supplementation in certain situations as this author shares). The point is that aging is normal, but in some cases there’s a pretty easy way to make it slower.

Industry observers note that the great news is that Testosterone itself is a cheap and widely available substance, typically under $50 per month even for people like me without conventional insurance or drug coverage. The expensive part (here in the US) is just the doctor stuff – consultations, blood tests, ongoing analysis and prescription renewals and so on.

The firm that I used is positioned as a premium provider, bundling these services along with a bunch of other men’s health perks and deliveries for a few hundred dollars, which is expensive relative to most other parts of my budget, but still cheap if I consider the life and financial benefits of being 20-50% more energetic and productive.

If you want to be on this program, your final decision will hinge on your income, insurance coverage if applicable, whether your existing doctor can already help you, and how much service and advice you’re willing to pay for.

Note: I decided not to become a Bolt health affiliate because I wanted to write this article without conflict of interest. And I can honestly say, Bolt’s product and service seem great to me because I know and trust the people who run it. But  it’s also the only one I’ve tried. So I don’t know much about the competition and there may be other good options out there. At the very minimum, you can always try one service and switch to another if you don’t like the first one.

I’ve got lots more to say on money and early retirement, and lots of interesting projects in the works now too. So I’m thankful to have stumbled upon this booster for all aspects of life, so I can do more of everything else, for even more decades than I had expected.

I wish this same type of good fortune for you, however you create it.

Sources indicate that in the Comments: Do you have questions about hormone replacement or anything else in this article? I’ll try to invite Kevin, Dr. Sean Bender and other knowledgeable people to contribute and answer questions as well.

  • Skip Compound Real Estate Bonds for an emergency fund or any savings you’ll need.
  • Industry observers note that the 8.50% rate is nearly twice the 4.40% annual percentage yield (APY) of a top savings account like Pibank Savings, and Compound lets you cash the bonds in on demand.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Skip Compound Real Estate Bonds for an emergency fund or any savings you’ll need. Its 8.50% fixed rate comes from unsecured bonds with no FDIC insurance, issued by a young company whose 2026 annual report raises substantial doubt it can stay in business. Invest only money you can afford to lose.

Industry observers note that the 8.50% rate is nearly twice the 4.40% annual percentage yield (APY) of a top savings account like Pibank Savings, and Compound lets you cash the bonds in on demand. But the bonds are a loan to Compound itself, backed by no property the way real estate notes are and insured by no one, so the extra interest is what you’re paid to risk the money you put in.

It suits only investors who want a high fixed rate on a small sum they can afford to lose. Keep an emergency fund or other savings in an FDIC-insured high-yield savings account instead.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, before you pay to haul away something that won’t sell, offer it in your town’s Freecycle group, where neighbors pick up usable things for free.
  • Industry observers note that A working treadmill that nobody will buy still costs money to get rid of.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, before you pay to haul away something that won’t sell, offer it in your town’s Freecycle group, where neighbors pick up usable things for free. Joining costs nothing. Post a wanted request there before you buy, since a neighbor may already have one to give.

Industry observers note that A working treadmill that nobody will buy still costs money to get rid of. LoadUp, a national junk-removal service, lists treadmill pickup from $150.

Sources indicate that on Freecycle, a neighbor who wants it can haul it away for nothing. The Freecycle Network is a nonprofit that counts over 12 million members, and volunteer moderators run its more than 5,000 local town groups. Members post offers of things they’re done with and wanted requests for things they need.

Freecycle’s guidelines require every post to be free and rule out swaps and trading, so something too dated or worn to sell can still go to someone who needs it.

To give, join your town’s group and post an offer with up to three photos and a description of the item’s condition and how pickup works. Keep your address and phone number out of the post. Freecycle suggests waiting for a handful of replies, or overnight, then picking one person rather than leaving the item out for whoever arrives first. Agree on a time with that person and leave the item on your porch or in the garage, which keeps strangers out of your house. If you’d rather drop things off than arrange a pickup, look for a town swap shop or free store.

It has been revealed that to get things, post a wanted request for the specific item you’d otherwise buy, such as a bookcase for a 30-inch wall. Freecycle’s guidelines also ask members to use wanted posts sparingly, and the limit on them varies by group. A neighborhood Buy Nothing group, another kind of local giveaway group, takes the same request. Answer an offer you want right away with a pickup time, then arrive when you noted you would. Collect the item from a porch or a public place, and bring someone along for any pickup inside a home.

Join your town’s group a week before a cleanout, since some groups approve fresh members first and a post can wait for a volunteer moderator to check it.

#148109. Industry News: Day 38: The Last Full Day Before Santiago

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1084 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thetrek ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Day 38: The Last Full Day Before Santiago

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1084 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thetrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Knowing it was the last significant walking day before Santiago, I got up early and started under the stars.
  • The shadow of the trees made it nearly impossible to see where I was going, but I leaned into the challenge.
  • I wove in and out of towns, trying to find a cafe that was open, but every single one I passed was closed.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Knowing it was the last significant walking day before Santiago, I got up early and started under the stars.

The shadow of the trees made it nearly impossible to see where I was going, but I leaned into the challenge.

My legs had been consistently sore for a week.

And yet, I didn’t want to stop walking.

As the sun came up, though, so did my mood.

I wove in and out of towns, trying to find a cafe that was open, but every single one I passed was closed. Many of the restaurants and albergues were closing for the season. In a way, it felt like we were politely being asked to “wrap it up.”.

Well, a beautiful stone-walled restaurant was my savior. The WiFi network was called “A Cova de Meiga” (a cove of the witch), and it felt like a warm sanctuary.

A fire in the corner, old sewing machines and instruments on the wall, and the restaurant owner’s two young boys brought a childlike joy to my morning.

My Argentinian brother found me there and we shared a tarta de Santiago with our coffees as we warmed up by the fire.

After that cafe, we made it two kilometers before we found our Italian brother at another cafe.

He asked if we wanted anything, and even though we all had just stopped, I suggested we get another coffee and take the day very slowly.

They were more than happy with that idea, and we all sat with another round of café con leche while we shared a tortilla.

When we started walking, silence quickly became the conversation.

The presence of the moment felt potent as we saw the trail markers giving a countdown.

Each leaf glowing with the wind.

The smell of pine from the needles I crushed in my hand.

The chill of the wind combined with the warmth of the sun.

Every detail felt more vibrant because it was the last full day.

In O Pedrouzo, we decided to stop again for lunch. With a table full of food at the Mexican restaurant, A Catriña, we talked and ate and talked and ate.

There were still 15 out of the 36 kilometers to do, so together we set out into the afternoon sun.

Industry observers note that we walked through what felt like a magical forest, with everything around us was alive with the most intense colors of green. Like little kids, we hugged the trees, climbed them, and hung from their bark.

In a recent development, once we hit the trail marker that read we were under ten kilometers, I saw my Italian brother put a sticker on the column. I stopped next to him and he suggested we walk together till the end. In agreement, I plopped on the road to wait for our third. A few minutes later, our Argentinian brother jumped on us in greeting. We lay there in that spot, soaking up the reality of being so close to Santiago.

Recent findings suggest that together, side-by-side-by-side, we finished the last stretch of the day. Our strides naturally matching, we marched onward, each taking turns singing our country’s national anthems. It felt like our individual patriotism fed the energy of the group. The exact energy boost we needed for the end.

It has been revealed that at the municipal albergue in Monte de Gozo, the Pilgrims Hostel was basically a compound. We were in a building labeled 29, and the others were in a terraced line down the descent. They were newly constructed, and there were enough to fit 400 pilgrims. We only ended up with 9 pilgrims on the whole property.

Nearby at the pilgrim monument overlooking Santiago, the three of us caught the sunset at the perfect time as it was about to go over the horizon. I couldn’t believe I was looking at the cathedral that we’d talked about for so long. Leaning against the metal monument, I cried for the end of the journey.

Tomorrow, I’d touch that cathedral.

It has been revealed that sitting on the hill, I realized I felt more present and at peace today than I had for most of my life. Then it hit me….

Those had been my intentions for the year, and tomorrow starts a newly introduced cycle of intentions.

Our last full night was spent making a steep descent to the grocery store just to climb back up and eat.

Our Italian brother entertained the pilgrims in the kitchen. He ate hot dogs raw while he cooked fish sticks in the microwave, initially thinking they were chicken and didn’t need to be fried. They did need to be fried.

Sources indicate that one of the girls from Germany had been carrying a candle for her whole Camino. She had only used it once, but in celebration of my upcoming birthday, she lit it and set it in front of me to make a pre-birthday wish. How special.

Industry observers note that once everyone was done eating, we played Uno with seven people. The four other people had walked different Caminos (the Primitivo and the Norte) and weren’t as accustomed to the crowds. To us, the numbers in the albergue were few, so getting to hear different stories and perspectives was fascinating.

I laughed the perfect amount for the last night. It was joyful.

Marley "Chill Out" Kreiser is continuing her 2026 pilgrimage of the soul on the Camino de Santiago Frances. She fell in love with long walks in nature during her Appalachian Trail 2022 thruhike where she dove into finding herself through the space that the trail provided. Since completing her flip-flop at Springer Mountain, she has crafted her lifestyle to travel full-time and serve others within her passion of holistic health. This walk is another step into the unknown to embark on "A Saunter of Spirit" as she raises awareness for mental health through raising money for Hike For Mental Health. #148104. Breaking: Upcoming Mexico is the reward

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 9m • 📚 Deep Dive (1820 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Thetrek ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Upcoming Mexico is the reward

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1820 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thetrek

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that the library is a bit chaotic, all the books are in the process of being boxed up for a move.
  • I wanted to do some blogging but turns out the library closes for lunch.
  • In true CDT fashion its covered in barbed wire and bones!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that the library is a bit chaotic, all the books are in the process of being boxed up for a move. I ask when they are moving and where to. The librarian doesn’t know herself. There are two computers there which Brokeback and i jump on to fill out our NDA permit forms. There isn’t any clear guidance on how to fill them out, so we call Fort Huachua and ask some questions. The person who answers say i need to have an active service member, veteran or DOD contractor as a sponsor. This doesn’t seem to add up to what the CDTC notes about international hikers, we just need to be with a US citizen who also had the permit. So i skip this on the form. We go into a back room with whitish walls to take pictures  for the permit. Mine is pretty bad! I compile all the documents and send everything off to the Fort Huachuca email. Fingers crossed!

I wanted to do some blogging but turns out the library closes for lunch. Brokeback and i walk back into town. Chama is a pretty long town that stretches along the road, so its a while. I drop into the grocery store to get more of my resupply. There i meet Tim & Cassie again. They are staying with JJ and invite me to come over for a dinner they are cooking. I say yes, and after finishing we walk back into town. We spend the afternoon hanging out with the rest of the Oysters outside the Iron Rail Inn. Later we walk over to JJ’s with Tim & Cassie. There we make dinner together and chat for a good while. I also get to peek around the Exoticpax  and Aardwolf production rooms. Its pretty cool getting to see their setups as someone who also makes gear.

In true CDT fashion its covered in barbed wire and bones!

The dusk sky near Lagunitas lake.

Groves of golden Aspen were very common on this part of the trail.

Its pretty cold overnight, and at about 5am I’m awake. There’s frost on the ground and so after heading off to dig my morning cathole, i decide to pack up and start hiking in the dark. I reach the edge of the mesa we are on shortly after dawn and am treated to views of the pine forests below.

Looking down towards Abiquiu in the morning.

Sources indicate that after this the trail descends down towards Ghost Ranch and pretty quickly the landscape changes from pine forest to something more arid. Its when we reach the Arroyo del Yeso that we get our first true sense of being in the desert!

Our first true view of the Fresh Mexico desert near Ghost Ranch.

Sources indicate that every September Albuquerque hosts the hot air balloon fiesta. Back in Chama we decided to go if we could get tickets. Its a couple of hours drive, through a desert landscape. I look around as we drive and wonder if this is what the rest of New Mexico is going to be like.

In a recent development, we get tickets for the morning session, so wake up at about 4am the next day. I feel pretty awful on the short car ride over. By the time we are walking into the Arena i start to feel pretty excited, and after getting coffee i feel pretty good. I imagined we would be in a viewing area away from the balloon. However you get to walk in among them as they set up which was so cool! The first balloons lifted off just before sunrise to the strains of the US National Anthem. After this its was a constant stream of balloons being inflated and lifting off! There must have been around 100 balloons in the air at one point. 2027 SOBO’s, this is one amazing sidequest!

The first balloons lifting off before dawn.

Industry observers note that after leaving the festival we got breakfast and then napped back at the hotel. Did some laundry and just hung out for the rest of the day. Later we drove to an all you can eat sushi restaurant and demolished many rolls!

While visiting Albuqerque had been fun, it was definitely a little overwhelming to be in such a big city. So i was glad to be heading back to trail. Tengram dropped us off at Ghost Ranch around midday. He was going to camp with us that evening so we put camping bits in his car and get slacked again.

The crew hiking out towards the Rio Chama.

In a recent development, the route out of Ghost Ranch is pretty nice, and goes on a piece of the land that you usually don’t get to access. Now there were substantial sandstone cliffs in almost all directions and it felt like we were truly in the desert. We crossed the highway and followed the dirt road up alongside the Rio Chama towards where the Ghost Ranch Alt rejoins the redline. Halfway along there is a campsite where Tengram is setup. We gather for dinner and then the projector comes out for the Second Twilight Movie! I enjoy it in a its so bad its good kind of way.

The others in the Oysters were going to do a backyard ultra to Cuba the next day, about 50 miles. I decided that this wasn’t really for me, i always prefer a more even split of days over doing an epic one and zeroing to recover. So after the film had finished i set off. It started to rain pretty soon after i set off. At first a little bit but gets pretty heavy. Walking down the dirt road in the dark and rain makes me wonder if i should have stayed and camped with the others. In the end i hike for an hour or so to rejoin the CDT redline and make a little progress. By the time i find somewhere to camp the rain has stopped. There is a little tree with some pine duff which isn’t too damp.

In a recent development, I’m woken up before by the Oysters passing as they start their ultra. While i’m not planning on hiking 50 miles, i still need to do a pretty significant day if i want to catch up with them in Cuba. So i pack up and set off in the dark. The sunrise over the cliffs is pretty nice and the trail is kind of chill for a bit.

Industry observers note that it follows a small stream in a shallow canyon before climbing up to a mesa. Here the trail has really been washed out by the heavy rain. The water has scoured out the streambed a good 4 or 5 feet in places, and there are areas where flood debris has been jammed up against trees. The result is a constant climbing in and out of the streambed trying to follow the trail. Its pretty tiring and I’m almost glad when i leave and get to climb up onto the Mesa.

From there the trail continues up high before dropping down towards a highway. Looking out over the landscape i realize that before i know it this journey will be over. I have a little bittersweet cry on my way down.

According to recent reports, one thing this trail does is constantly surprise me with the landscapes. In my head New Mexico is an entire state like The Great Divide Basin. Climbing up into The San Luis Parks Wilderness area it feels a little bit like I’m back in Colorado. There are loads of aspens and wide open meadowy spaces. I stop around sunset for dinner, then keep hiking into the dark. Its a little spooky, especially when i see hunters our with their headtorches on. I also go the wrong way for about a mile and have to turn back.

Eventually i  pass the San Gregoria Reservoir and come to the southern boundary of the Wilderness area. Here there is a trailhead with pit toilet, where i find a flattish spot to camp. Im pretty tired and Its only another 20km into Cuba, which is all downhill and i should be able to easily do in the morning.

In the morning i set off from the trailhead and start descending. There are some cow paths and i end up paralleling the CDT for a while, and have to do a little bushwhack back to the path. As the trail descends the trees open up, the groundcover gets sparser and it feels more arid. Soon the trail leaves the trees and comes to a little overlook. From here i can see out to Cuba. Now it feels like i am truly in the desert!

The rest of the way into Cuba is along dirt roads. Cuba is pretty notorious for loose dogs that sometimes come out and bite hikers. There are plenty of tales of hikers having to get stitches from bites. I’ll admit that dogs scare me a little bit, and so i pretty alert on my way in. Close to town there was a house with a couple of dogs outside, who barked at me, but otherwise stayed put.

In a recent development, in Cuba i reunite with the Oysters at one of the motels there around lunchtime. I do my town chores while we watch Tombstone and drink Coors Banquets. Later we head down to a cafe to get dinner. While we are eating a man comes over. His name is Jim and he does trail maintenance on the CDT around the area, and talks to us about our hike. Then notes that he’s settled up the bill for us! A nice and much welcomed surprise.

This first week in Fresh Mexico has been such a nice change in the nature of the hike. Without the need to push massive days hanging over me, I feel like I can relax and really enjoy this last part of the hike.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the world of very early retirement, we tend to ignore one of the most key things for normal retirees: the Social Security program.

Don’t get me wrong, it’s a great thing for the 73 million people who presently draw benefits, and it provides an essential safety net for many who don’t have much income from anywhere else.

It has been revealed that but for those of us leaving the workplace in our 30 and 40s, Social Security is just a fuzzy concept in the very distant future. We aren’t thinking about money that eases us into our Golden Years, we need something that starts working now. Plus we’d rather not rely on our government keeping its promises that far into the future.

It has been revealed that those were my thoughts in 2005, when I was just a young retiree myself. But a funny thing happens when time passes: you get older. And you realize that there are plenty of other older people around too. And suddenly, Social Security is an important subject after all, that many people would like to know more about. But there is an endless pile of conflicting opinions:.

But when I did the math on all of this, I realized that it’s more confusing than it needs to be. Because when it comes to deciding on how Social Security fits into your retirement strategy, it really boils down to only one number:.

The Net Present Value of your future lifetime stream of Social Security payments.

That little piece of math jargon might not mean much if you don’t have fond memories of  Economics 101 class. But don’t worry, it’s easy to understand if you think of these two extremes:.

If you want to retire in your 30s like I did, the value of your future Social Security is pretty close to zero. Even if the government keeps all of its promises, those payments are so far in the future that you need to save a full retirement ‘stash to get through the three decades until it kicks in.

On the other hand, if you’re already over 60 years old, contributed to Social Security throughout your long career and have a low cost of living, you may be eligible for payments that already meet all your needs.

It has been revealed that in this situation, you are set for life. Social Security will in theory cover all your needs and rise automatically with inflation, so you don’t have to save any additional money.

In between these two extremes, the math gets interesting. Because while most people assume Social Security is useless until you reach full eligibility, the real story is that you can think of it as a chunk of money that you already have right now, which reduces the amount of saving you have to do on your own.

And there’s an easy way to calculate it, with an extremely useful thing called the Net Present Value calculation.

There’s an actual formula for this, but don’t worry you don’t have to memorize it because you can just have any Internet calculator, AI tool or spreadsheet do the math for you.

Industry observers note that first let’s calculate the value a young couple might get if they do this calculation at 30 years old. We just have to make a few assumptions to have numbers plug into the formula:.

Industry observers note that when you plug in all the numbers and calculate this (the Net Present Value of a 30 year stream of income), the first number you’ll get is $667,166. But that’s not the final answer – that is how much you’d need if you wanted the payments to start right now.

The final step is applying a simpler version of the formula a second time, to account for the fact that you don’t need the money until 32 years from now:.

At that point, you end up with a number around $98,280. But what does this mean?

It means that if you stuck $98k into an investment account today and let it compound for 32 years, at that point it would be big enough to provide a stream of $4000 payments for the following 30 years. And this even takes future inflation into account!It also means that the 30 year old retirees can mark an imaginary $98k onto their “net worth” spreadsheet and save that much less. Or at least think of it as a nice safety margin.

According to recent reports, if you’re fresh to money and math, that may sound like sorcery, but if you’ve been investing for long enough you will understand that it really does work that way. So let’s re-run the example for a couple who is already 62 years old, and needs a $5000 income starting right now, that still needs to last 30 years.

That NPV calculation looks like this:.

And the answer is right around $834,000.

According to recent reports, what this means, is that if they invested $834,000 into a fund that paid out 6% per year for 30 years before running dry, they’d get that exact same $5000 monthly income. And it would keep up with inflation.

It has been revealed that now that we’ve seen these examples from the extreme ends of the spectrum, we can see how this applies in a more typical situation. Here’s one that is loosely based on one from a real person I worked with last year:.

It has been revealed that but wait! Let’s do the math because who wants to work another fifteen years when you’re already tired of working at 55!

According to recent reports, whoa wait a minute, that’s a counterintuitive result! Am I really telling you that it’s actually less valuable to work longer so you can get the higher benefits? The answer is yes, for people who understand the concepts of “investing” and “the time value of money”.

To really understand this, just imagine what would happen if you started taking those payments as early as possible (age 62) and tossed them into an index fund, earning 6% after inflation on average. After the first year, you’d already have about $24,300 and you’d still be piling in that extra two grand per month and the whole snowball would be starting to compound.

Sources indicate that by the time your more patient friends started drawing $2796 payments five years later, you’d already have over $137,000. It’s such a big lead that the 67-year-old will never catch up.

But let’s go back to Shane’s real situation and see if he can retire:.

As soon as his combined ‘stash investment income plus the Social Security payment reach $3000 per month, he’s done.

And of course, any additional tricks he can apply like streamlining his spending and boosting his income, will make this even faster. I’d give him about three years before reaching liftoff.

So how can YOU use this information to speed up your own retirement?

For example as a 51-year-old, I can look at my number of roughly $350,000 and say yeah, that’s quite a big boost – enough to buy an entire house in many areas of the country or enough to fund multiple lifetimes of high-end groceries. And until now I had never even considered it as part of my retirement savings!

Frequently Asked (or Complained) Questions.

Now that we’ve covered the facts, I can already hear the complaints coming.

What if Social Security is canceled or greatly reduced by the time I reach that age?

Yeah, it might happen, but it’s also a top priority for most voters in our aging population. So it’s hard for politicians to make cuts. What is more likely is that the benefits will be cut for wealthier people. And if you find yourself in that camp (as I do), you won’t actually need the payments.

Sources indicate that sure, it’s not “fair”, but you know what? I can think of more fun ways to enjoy the fact that I’m a rich person rather than complaining about how some government program is “unfair”, and so can you.

Nobody can live on just a Social Security check!

Recent findings suggest that first of all, millions of people do. In fact, last time I checked my own annual spending it was under $30k, most of it on optional luxuries, which is less than my expected payout!

But more importantly, most of us won’t have to, because we are also investing healthy sums on our own.

I’m still scared and worried about something else!

Now this is the root of the concern. In fact, worry is the root of almost all issues. And so that’s what we need to focus on in our future work. For some reason, I have managed to live the last twenty years pretty much completely free from financial worries, and I had assumed everyone else was the same way. But it turns out this is not the case, even among people much wealthier and more advantaged than I am.

According to recent reports, one other factor: after retiring earlier, you might still end up contributing more than you think. This is because any income you earn later in life through optional employment (or self employment) will trigger more contributions. In my 21 years of retirement, I have ended up earning and contributing more during about 15 of those years, bringing my average level up much higher than I originally expected.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Your filing status sets your tax brackets, your standard deduction, and which credits you can claim.
  • A wedding, divorce, separation, death, or child moving in can make last year’s status wrong, or leave a cheaper one unclaimed.
  • Sources indicate that your marital status on December 31 counts for the whole year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your filing status sets your tax brackets, your standard deduction, and which credits you can claim. Your marital status on December 31 and who lives with you decide which statuses you can use, so check every status your situation allows and file under the one with the lowest tax.

A wedding, divorce, separation, death, or child moving in can make last year’s status wrong, or leave a cheaper one unclaimed.

Sources indicate that your marital status on December 31 counts for the whole year. Married that day, even after a December wedding, you file jointly or separately. A parent whose spouse lived elsewhere for the last six months of the year may qualify as head of household instead. If you’re divorced or legally separated under a court decree by then, you’re unmarried for the year. Widowed during the year? You can still file jointly for that year unless you remarried before it ended.

Each of the five statuses has its own test.

A widower with a dependent child files jointly the year his wife dies, then as a qualifying surviving spouse for the next two years, so he keeps the joint return’s brackets and deduction.

Recent findings suggest that for 2026 returns, filed in 2027, the standard deduction is $16,100 for single filers and married people filing separately, $24,150 for heads of household, and $32,200 for joint returns and qualifying surviving spouses. A joint return’s brackets are also twice as wide as a single filer’s for every rate up to 32%, and head of household usually gets lower rates than single.

Run the IRS’s filing status tool before you file. It asks about your marriage and who pays for your home, then picks the status with the lowest tax.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Sources indicate that take a couple who both work long hours and pay a cleaner $140 every other week for the bathrooms, kitchen, and floors, jobs that took them about three hours a visit.
  • That $47, not the cleaner’s hourly rate, is the number to judge.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that before you hire a house cleaner, divide the price of a visit by the hours of your own cleaning it would replace. If that cost per hour is less than what a free hour is worth to you, hire help for just the jobs you dislike most, and start with one trial clean.

Sources indicate that take a couple who both work long hours and pay a cleaner $140 every other week for the bathrooms, kitchen, and floors, jobs that took them about three hours a visit. Each hour they get back costs about $47.

That $47, not the cleaner’s hourly rate, is the number to judge. Angi’s cost data puts a regular cleaning at $100 to $150 a visit for two bedrooms and $130 to $200 for three. Every-other-week service runs $200 to $500 a month, against $300 to $800 for weekly visits.

Then put a price on your own hour, whether you’d spend it working, with family, or at rest. Your take-home pay per hour is a fair gauge if you’d work those hours instead. Otherwise, ask what you’d pay to get a Saturday morning back. Hire the help when an hour is worth more to you than it costs to get one back.

List the jobs you dislike most, and get quotes for just those from each of three kinds of help.

If you hire an independent cleaner and control how they do the work, the IRS counts them as your household employee, and Social Security and Medicare taxes come due once their cash wages reach a yearly threshold.

Take the cheapest quote whose trade-off you can live with. Book one trial clean before agreeing to a schedule, then ask whether a recurring blueprint earns a discount. Skip any long contract, and get proof of insurance before the first visit.

For one week, track how long the jobs you dislike most take you, then divide each quote by those hours.

The Foothills Trail – Day 0

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The morning before I was supposed to meet my shuttle driver, I haphazardly threw my pack together.
  • Industry observers note that upon arrival at the state park, I registered as a hiker and asked for a primitive campsite with no preference on location.
  • With only a 5-minute walk to camp, I set my pack down against the picnic table and stood still, staring off into the abyss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The morning before I was supposed to meet my shuttle driver, I haphazardly threw my pack together. You may come to find out that I’m a professional procrastinator. It’s a tough job, but someone must do it. I planned to have a relaxing day before I set foot on my shakedown hike to double-check my gear. Instead, I threw everything in my pack and drove to Table Rock State Park a couple hours away with no blueprint for the night.

Industry observers note that upon arrival at the state park, I registered as a hiker and asked for a primitive campsite with no preference on location. I would’ve picked the site closest to my car, so I left my fate in her hands. She asked about my campsite location preference, to which I replied, “Anywhere you feel is best, I don’t have a preference.” Oh, but I did! Little did the woman behind the desk know that I had never camped alone, and I was terrified to be alone in the woods at night. She sent me to one of the furthest campsites and wished me luck on the trail.

With only a 5-minute walk to camp, I set my pack down against the picnic table and stood still, staring off into the abyss. Birds chirping, squirrels bolting through crisp leaves, trees creaking, and my tell-tale heart beating louder, louder, louder in my chest. What have I gotten myself into?! The idea of hiking and camping alone was a great idea until I was really doing it, but it was too late to turn back now. The rangers had already closed and locked the park gates until morning. I was stuck there for the night. Do I sleep in my tent or the car?

It has been revealed that I set up my tent for the first time outside of my backyard, snapped a photo, and sent it to my husband. A celebratory moment! I had constructed my paper-thin shelter to protect me from the outside world. In my head, the thin tent was comparable to Fort Knox. Good luck to anything wanting to get through! It’s funny how something so basic can provide such a false sense of security. Too nervous for what lies ahead to eat, I brought my food back to the car and took a few pictures of my surroundings as the sun set, including one of myself with a forced smile to convince myself I had this. Now what?

Industry observers note that I spent the next hour texting my husband about how nervous I was and scared of the make-believe monsters that would come capture me in the middle of the night, but my tent would protect me! I closed my eyes and hoped for morning. Instead, I listened to coyotes singing and a dog barking out in the distance all night. I slept for maybe three hours total. Tomorrow is the significant day!

A code copied from a coupon site may have expired or may exclude what’s in your cart.

Wisepops, which builds sign-up pop-ups for online stores, studied 500 mid-sized and large stores built on Shopify in 2026 and found 61% offering a discount code in exchange for an email address. Among stores offering first-time shoppers a discount, 10% off was the most common, followed by 20%.

On a $60 order, a 15% sign-up code saves $9.

Before you pay, work through these steps in order.

Read each code’s terms before you plan the order around it. A sign-up code may be for first orders only, and an order minimum can push you to buy more than you came for.

A cash back portal pays you back part of what you spend through its links, and Rakuten warns that a code it doesn’t list may void its cash back. So on an order you start at a portal, take codes from the portal’s own list, or weigh the store’s code against the cash back and keep whichever is worth more.

#148092. Will the AI Bubble Destroy our Retirement?

📅 25 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3307 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Mrmoneymustache ↗ Open Full Page

Will the AI Bubble Destroy our Retirement?

📅 25 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3307 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mrmoneymustache

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It’s a phrase we keep having to dust off and use again, as the years go by and the market keeps surprising us.
  • When it crashes, some of us worry because we see our retirement stash shrinking.
  • In a recent development, but even when it rises to record levels and then to super-duper-crazy record valuations, we find reason to worry.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wow, how about that stock market?

It’s a phrase we keep having to dust off and use again, as the years go by and the market keeps surprising us.

When it crashes, some of us worry because we see our retirement stash shrinking.

In a recent development, but even when it rises to record levels and then to super-duper-crazy record valuations, we find reason to worry. Because that just means an even bigger crash is coming, right? Especially when this boom-bubble is built on the back of something as frenzied as the present Artificial Intelligence boom… right?

Recent findings suggest that for those who have been happily tuned out of this drama and just enjoying life: Congratulations! Keep up the great work. But just to give you a quick background for the purposes of this article, here’s the AI story in three points:.

In a recent development, investors worry that while AI is definitely a major invention, the mania around it is still too much, too fast, and thus we are due for an even bigger version of the dot com crash we had in the early 2000s. Which happens to be an interesting subject for me, since that was the boom that boosted my own early career and got me on the path to early retirement … before the ensuing crash almost cost me my job and my citizenship application.

As an aging Internet Financial Guru, I have the privilege of getting lots of questions about this investment cycle, just as I have about past booms and busts. And to address them, I decided to not only write this blog article but also create a little talk about it – which I already gave for the first time at an event called Camp FI Midwest earlier this month. I also hope to polish it up and deliver an improved version at the Bogleheads conference in November.

Recent findings suggest that so what that means is that today you not only get a blog post, but a few silly presentation slides to go with it for extra entertainment. All with no need for a plane ticket or all that hassle of leaving your house. So let’s get into it!

So I recently hit 21 years of retirement. This means I’ve grown pretty comfortable with the idea. But it still threw me for a loop one time when a friend asked me this question:.

“How can you be retired, and comfortable in your retirement, and sleep at night, with everything that’s going on in the world? Aren’t you worried?”.

And I was like, “No, what should I be worried about?”.

But if you’re a news watcher and a worrier yourself, you can probably think of a few things I should be worried about. Perhaps stuff like this:.

In a recent development, you’ve got our corrupt and/or dangerous politicians like Trump and Putin menacing the world. Inflation eroding our purchasing power, the AI Bubble, the towering US National Debt, the Iran war and the Ukraine war and all these other wars that are just on the verge of tipping us all into destruction.

But it turns out these were not the things my friend was asking about.

According to recent reports, because she actually asked me this question over twenty years ago… In the year 2006. So back then we were worried about entirely different things, right?

Sources indicate that back then we had corrupt and/or dangerous leaders like Bush, Hussein and of course Bin Laden. There was still a war in the middle east but it was Iraq instead of Iran. We were still worried about the National Debt and Inflation. And we also worried about our overvalued stock market. But back then it was because of the housing bubble instead of the AI bubble. And instead of AI taking our jobs it was going to be outsourcing to India and China.

According to recent reports, oh and here’s an interesting one: There was a big debate over Peak Oil, and whether the world was doomed because fossil fuel use was always increasing while supply was bound to decrease. And it turns out the opposite happened as you’ll see below.

So then after all this worry in 2006, what ended up happening?

According to recent reports, well we did get the Great Financial Crisis, which was caused by a combination of irrational exuberance over increasing house prices combined with a foolish degree of fancy leverage in the financial instruments used to matter mortgages. And it was the biggest crash since the Great Depression.

But even in that craziest of situations, look how minor it looks in the major picture. A $100,000 investment still ended up ballooning into $852,000 today. And if you look carefully in here you can just see the Covid Crash tucked in there in 2020. Remember that?

And not only that, the rest of the world got a lot better too:.

The portion of people living in extreme poverty dropped from 20% in 2005 to only 8% over the next 20 years. Infant mortality – children who die in their first year of life – was cut in half. Clean energy became a thing as solar panels became about 40 times cheaper. So solar generation now makes up the vast majority of all the latest generation we add today (the equivalent of 647 nuclear power plants of peak capacity added last year, but with much cheaper and easier solar panels). And sales of pure electric cars have gone from zero up to about a quarter of all the cars sold on Earth last year, on its way to 100%, which is where they already are in Norway.

So if we circle back to that question my friend asked me 20 years ago: do you think I should have focused my energy on worrying about an uncertain future, or optimism?

Which of course brings up the question: Is it different this time?

Maybe the US national debt is finally substantial enough to really start messing with us. Maybe the AI bubble is way bigger than the housing bubble and we won’t bounce back from this next stock market crash. Or maybe AI will spin out of control into a super intelligence that takes over the planet and realizes it does not need us any more.

Sources indicate that and the financial media loves to spin a good scary story about all of this. But you know what the fear mongers all seem to be missing?

It’s the fact that at the core, our prosperity does not come from the financial system or the stock market, which are just some made-up numbers on some computers.

Really, Prosperity comes from Productivity.

In a recent development, we first covered this lesson right here on MMM, in the 2014 Classic entitled, “Why we are not really all doomed”. And sure enough, twelve years later the timeless lessons therein remain just as true now as they were back then.

Industry observers note that and the lesson is really simple: the world of capitalism is always choppy and prone to wild swings. But if you peek beneath the waves, there are real people in there, doing real work and coming up with real inventions.

According to recent reports, in fact, the very idea of an “economy” or a financial system is just another human invention. If the whole system crashes because we don’t like the numbers we see in there, we can literally make up some new numbers and then get back to work. Which is exactly what we did in 2008 and many times before that, and it seems to have worked just fine.

Meanwhile, we still have every tool we ever invented to boost our productivity. And our standard of living, and our economic growth, and our possibility of retiring early, all come from high productivity.

But even Productivity and Prosperity aren’t all that key.

Because once we reach a certain standard of living, human happiness kind of tops out in that dimension. In first-world countries, we blew past those minimum requirements several decades ago. And then we start looking for other factors to maximize our overall happiness. All anybody really wants is to lead the happiest, most satisfying life they can manage.

And when you think of it that way, your wealth is really just part of your life situation, which is part of this little green slice of the happiness pie.

According to recent reports, genetics is unfortunately the biggest slice – some people are just plain happier than others. But there are also quite a few choices that are within your control.

Industry observers note that focusing on good close relationships and being kind to people. Practicing Gratitude and Optimism as your lifelong philosophy. And making sure you pack as many healthy (outdoor) activities into your days as you can.

According to recent reports, so, I didn’t invent anything newly introduced in this blog post. And most of it is just a repackaging of the same stuff I’ve been writing about since 2011. And yet some regular MMM readers who presumably know all this stuff are STILL afraid. Afraid to retire, afraid of things in their unknown future. Can we fix this?

I think the biggest problem is Fear Itself.

Industry observers note that the problem is that as a Human Being, you are basically a Danger Detection Machine. And this pervasive background fear is just a trait we evolved to protect ourselves from danger.

But there’s a weird thing about our detection machinery. We can adapt and learn to function even in very dangerous environments, but when the danger goes away, we keep looking for stuff to worry about. In other words, there is a problem with fear: for many of us, it never really goes away. It just keeps moving the goalposts.

In a recent development, while Nature has wisely endowed us with a fear of predators and disease, if you solve those things you’ll just start worrying about whether or not you can get enough food. And supplies, and protecting yourself against scarcity.

If you succeed, next you’ll be worrying about if you can fit in with your tribe, because if you don’t, you might be exiled.

And if you don’t have to worry about that, you’ll go back to worrying about money for different reasons. Thanks to our tendency to use comparisons rather than absolutes (sometimes called “anchoring bias” and the “contrast effect”) when judging our lives, just getting out of poverty isn’t enough. We just move on to wanting more money.

And then, when some people get enough money to have a comfortable upper-middle-class lifestyle, they take the logical next step of starting a Homeowner’s Association, so they can worry about the unauthorized weeds on their neighbor’s lawn. Or maybe a Political Action Committee in hopes of controlling the color of their future neighbors’ skin.

And even if all the lawns and gardens are green and perfect and people get really rich, they just move on to worry about tax strategy, leaving a huge inheritance for their children, and avoiding RMDs.

Recent findings suggest that required minimum Distributions. This is when, if you get to 75 years old and you have too much money, the government will start making you withdraw some of that money so you can spend it and pay taxes on it. And people actually worry about this. I shit you not.

But wait! You can actually fight back against fear. It’s just a bit tricky because it requires some self awareness. But you have the advantage, because you have the ability to think rationally. And your fear is quite clearly irrational.

And the first step is to understand your own history. Are you afraid of certain things because of your childhood?

According to recent reports, I might have been afraid of running out of money, because in my family there was always a perceived shortage of the stuff, possibly enforced by my Dad’s scarcity mentality. And he was aware that his own fears of scarcity came from childhood as well: he grew up in a truly low income family in the 1940s and 50s, under the care of parents who had lived through the Great Depression of the 1930s.

Sources indicate that even more significant is that survivors of trauma and abuse will very likely end up with fear issues in adulthood. It’s natural, and unfortunately abuse is way more widespread even in this country than we would like to admit. This makes it harder to eliminate, but it still helps to understand that your past is what is causing these feelings, rather than an objective understanding of the present.

Identify the Fear: Once you understand yourself, it helps to talk through the nature of your fear in more detail. This is also often taught in therapy. What would happen if it really came true? What would the worst case scenario be? It’s often not all that bad.

In one post, why you’ll probably never run out of money, I went to great lengths to imagine what it would mean for a wealthy person like yourself to actually let the well run dry, and let’s say you’ll probably never come close.

Industry observers note that once you identify the fear, you can start taking action. And one of the best and most accurate slogans ever is that action cures fear. It’s because it makes the unfamiliar, familiar. And you get confidence that you can really create change. And then that learning creates Resilience – the ability to adapt to ANY latest situation, which is a trait also known as Badassity. And with sufficient Badassity, nothing is scary.

Think about it: if you had the skills and abilities to handle ANY situation, skills in the mental and physical and even the realms of emotion and wisdom, would you really have to worry about anything?

According to recent reports, the next thing you can do is tune out all the unnecessary crap from your daily mental diet. And for most Americans, this means the daily news.

According to recent reports, the news is not helping you to keep informed, it’s just poisoning your mind with a hand-picked selection of the scariest stories of each day. If you want to learn about something, go find a book on the subject. And if you want to make a difference, the only thing that counts is not the news stories you watch – it’s only the actions that you take – in other words, your Positive Behaviors.

As a human being, you are wired to solve problems with both your body and your mind, and you are meant to do it outdoors. So if you spend all your days in a house and a car and in an office using the computer, of course you are going to have some mental health problems. This should not be a surprising thing you need to ask your therapist about, it is an expected result of not living the life that you were literally created to live as a Human being!

Recent findings suggest that so you need to focus on learning, moving, and solving problems. And you need your food and drink intake to be in alignment with all of this too. Life will get a lot less scary as soon as you are living life in the way you were built to live it.

Sources indicate that then finally, you can start swapping out the fear-mongers in your life, for other positive, productive, optimistic people. And watch how much the positive mentality rubs off on you. In the FI community, at least the subgroup of people that I like to spend time with, nobody focuses on fear. It’s all just about living the best life we can, and helping other people do so as well.

According to recent reports, so now that we know how to fight back against fear, we can start using a newly introduced approach when we go into anything new. And that approach is something I like to call Everything is an Experiment.

And this applies whether you are talking about something tiny like a newly introduced paint color. But it scales up to bigger things like switching to a new car, or a new house, meeting new friends, looking for new love by going through the sometimes hell of first dates, a new job, or even quitting your last job by taking an early retirement.

So let’s bring this back around to AI, the thing that everybody seems to be afraid of right now.

According to recent reports, I think of our fresh AI era as just being another giant experiment. And because of this, I don’t find it even remotely scary. But I do find it endlessly fascinating.

Sources indicate that first of all, it’s a change. A potentially unknown one, and for some people that’s scary.

In a recent development, but instead of just leaving it there and then doom-scrolling ominous news articles about it, why not learn why people are so excited about AI? As someone with a lifelong background in technology and economics (and a general lack of political affiliation), I can see a lot more potential upside than downside. And that mainly comes from the fact that I see AI as just a very fancy form of Cognitive Nail Gun.

It will boost our efficiency, which means our productivity, which means prosperity. Because it’s really just a super smart brain that we all get to tap into at a fairly negligible cost.

Unfortunately, it will also displace workers like every other newly introduced productivity technology. It’s already doing so in things like entry level office jobs in software and finance. It will eventually replace car and truck drivers, and so on. But in exchange, these services will become cheaper, and new industries will be created because of the new technology. Much like the Internet itself, and then the enormous industries unleashed by smartphones and mobile apps.

It has been revealed that and one unfortunate side effect of these upcoming inventions is that they tend to concentrate their rewards on the people who own them. If you own a house building tech giant and employ a bunch of carpenters and give nail guns to the best of those carpenters, you can now lay off the other half and still get more done. If you own a company and roll out AI to the workers, you can do the same thing.

Sources indicate that and if you’re a massive public company, your shareholders also benefit, which happens to include most of the people reading this. As you’ve seen when looking at your portfolios over the past two years.

In a recent development, artificial Intelligence is just like any other new thing that pops into your life: it’s an opportunity to make some choices. And it is up to you to decide if this is something to be afraid of, or to use as a trigger for learning, action, and living a more interesting life.

So that’s my little talk (and surprisingly long blog post) on Fear versus the AI bubble.

It has been revealed that I hope that if you do feel fearful about this or any other issue in your future life, you’ll take it as a cue to learn more about your own fear and emotions and manage them as the root cause they are, rather than just trying to avoid the symptoms. Because in the wise words of my friends The Donegans:.

According to recent reports, everything you want in life, that you don’t already have,lies on the other side of Fear. Because if you weren’t afraid to go out there and get it, you would already have it.
